🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican Industry Grows for a Third Straight Month</u>

Industrial activity rose 0.6% in August and 3.6% year on year, INEGI reports, according to El Economista. That makes three straight months of growth. Construction led with +7.9% annually and manufacturing added 3.2%. Manufacturing and electricity each grew 1.2% from July; mining was the only sector to fall.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Indigenous Communities Asked for More Time. Sheinbaum Gave It</u>

President Sheinbaum will extend the consultation on the General Law on the Rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Peoples, at the request of the communities themselves, which say several points are still unresolved. She set no date for sending the bill to Congress: the law goes when the peoples agree on it, not before. Consultations have been underway since July.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ICE Agents Run Over a Mexican Migrant in Houston</u>

An unmarked ICE vehicle hit Mexican national Miguel Parra-Hernández during a raid near Houston on Saturday, breaking his leg as he fled on foot. ICE itself confirmed the vehicle carried no official identification. The man running with him, José Mendoza-Cervantes, has not been located. Houston is the same city where ICE shot and killed another Mexican, Lorenzo Salgado, in July.
banner: HOUSTON: ICE RUNS OVER MEXICAN MIGRANT

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum to Lemus: Explain the Tear Gas</u>

President Sheinbaum told Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus to explain why his police met a clean-water march in Guadalajara with tear gas and water cannons: "We do not agree with repression." 39 people were detained; 12 have been released. She also rejected any privatization of Jalisco's water service and announced a meeting between the state government and Conagua to work out alternatives.
banner: SHEINBAUM TO LEMUS: EXPLAIN THE TEAR GAS

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Tamaulipas Leads Mexico in Industrial Growth: +15.7%</u>

INEGI's state industrial-activity index puts Tamaulipas first in the country for June 2026, with growth of 15.7% from a year earlier and 13.7% from May, also the top monthly gain. Mining was up 107.4%, and manufacturing and construction also grew. Hidalgo (15.4%), Colima (13.4%), Veracruz (7.8%) and Yucatán (7.5%) round out the top five. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🏙️ <u>No Property Tax Hike in Mexico City. The PAN Bet on Panic</u>

The PAN warned that Mexico City's new metropolitan zoning program would bring higher property valuations, a tax on "underused" land and forced sales. Mayor Clara Brugada answered that property tax won't go up: "Let it be very clear, don't be deceived." Morena says the program creates no new taxes and authorizes no expropriations, and its Mexico City leadership calls the PAN's campaign "a bet on panic, fear and disinformation."

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>120 Pesos for a Copy That Costs 76 Cents: Supreme Court Moves to End Abusive Municipal Fees</u>

In San Pablo Macuiltianguis, Oaxaca, a municipality charged 120 pesos for a copy of an archive document whose real cost was 76 centavos, 158 times more. Mexico's Supreme Court kept striking down fees like these, but municipalities reset their rates every year and the same cases came back. Now the Court has a digital tool, the "Ecosystem of the Real Cost of State Services," which calculates what certified copies, street lighting, construction licenses, water supply and permits actually cost and flags fees that are out of line.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>"No Is No," Said the PAN. Now It's Talking to the PRI Again</u>

A year ago PAN leader Jorge Romero swore off the alliance with the PRI that sank them in 2024: asked about it on the radio, his answer was "no is no." With 2027 approaching, Romero now confirms advanced talks with the PRI for Nuevo León and Chihuahua, and PAN and PRI members in at least a dozen states want the PRIAN back. His justification: "if an alliance is going to be the factor to stop the growth of the guinda cancer, of course we'll take it."
banner: PAN: 'NO IS NO' TO PRI… NOW YES

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>US Gas Now Covers 74.6% of Mexico's Demand</u>

Mexico imported a record 7,636 million cubic feet of US natural gas per day in June, and for the first time May, June and July all topped 7,000, El Economista reports from EIA data. In 2025, imported gas met a record 74.6% of national demand, up from 39.7% in 2014, the year Peña Nieto's energy reform took effect, while Pemex's own output kept falling. Last week's 20% cut in US pipeline flows showed the cost: Mexico has almost no gas storage.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Guadalajara Marches for Clean Water. Lemus Answers With Tear Gas</u>

Thousands marched to Casa Jalisco on Sunday demanding clean water. Since March, at least 320 Guadalajara neighborhoods have been getting water contaminated with heavy metals and fecal matter. Movimiento Ciudadano Governor Pablo Lemus's state police met them with water cannons and tear gas. A journalist was hit in the face by a gas canister, and protesters were detained. This came days after the federal government agreed to pay 100% of the Zapotillo water works. Morena's national leadership demanded the detainees' release and real dialogue: "Repression should never be a government's response to social discontent."
banner: GUADALAJARA: WATER MARCH MET WITH TEAR GAS
